facts.fact_text: On 8 March 2005 the applicants took part in International Women's Day celebrations in the city of Malatya.
During the International Women's Day celebrations on 8 March 2005 in Malatya, a group comprising hundreds of police officers formed a cordon around the crowd.
During the International Women's Day celebrations on 8 March 2005 in Malatya, the police chief warned the participants that no prior permission had been obtained for the gathering.
According to the Government's submissions, the group of demonstrators, including the applicants, refused to disperse and continued with their demonstration on 8 March 2005.
According to the Government's submissions, the group of demonstrators insisted on blocking the street and continued with their demonstration on 8 March 2005.

Police officers dragged a number of persons, including four of the applicants, into waiting police vehicles.
In the course of dragging persons into police vehicles, police officers sprayed the crowds with tear gas.
In the course of dragging persons into police vehicles, police officers hit some of the crowd, including four of the applicants.
The four arrested applicants were taken to a police station on 8 March 2005.
Later on 8 March 2005, the four arrested applicants were released from police custody.
During the International Women's Day celebrations on 8 March 2005 in Malatya, the police chief warned the participants that no prior permission had been obtained for the gathering.
The first applicant, Ms Nihal Pekaslan, told the police chief that the applicable legislation required no prior permission for the gathering.
According to the Government's submissions, the demonstrations at the International Women's Day celebrations in Malatya on 8 March 2005 hindered the flow of traffic.

According to the Government's submissions, the police chief told the participants on 8 March 2005 that they could carry on with their demonstration on the pavement and walk in an orderly manner without violating public order.
According to the Government's submissions, the force used to put the persons into the police vehicles could not be considered disproportionate.
According to medical reports drawn up on 8 March 2005, the four applicants who had been hit by police officers had a number of injuries on their bodies.
According to medical reports drawn up on 8 March 2005, the injuries sustained by the four applicants rendered them unable to work for periods of between one and three days.

According to the medical report of 8 March 2005, Ms Nihal Pekaslan had four ecchymosed areas measuring between one and five centimetres on both forearms and on the left hand, and grazes on both forearms and on the left hand.

According to the doctor at the Malatya State Hospital, the injuries observed on the first applicant, Ms Nihal Pekaslan, on 10 March 2005 had been caused some thirty-six to forty-eight hours previously.

Between 4 April 2005 and 3 May 2005 the Malatya prosecutor took statements from eighteen police officers who had been on duty on the day of the incidents on 8 March 2005.
A police chief told the Malatya prosecutor that female demonstrators had attacked the police on 8 March 2005 and that the police had had to use force in response.
A police chief told the Malatya prosecutor that the force used by the police on 8 March 2005 had been proportionate.
Four of the police officers told the Malatya prosecutor that the demonstrators had blocked the street on 8 March 2005 and that the police had had to arrest them.

Four of the police officers told the Malatya prosecutor that while they were arresting the demonstrators on 8 March 2005 there had been scuffles and the demonstrators had attacked the police officers with sticks.
Four of the police officers told the Malatya prosecutor that the police officers had had to use force on 8 March 2005, as a result of which the demonstrators might have suffered minor injuries.

The remaining thirteen police officers' statements to the Malatya prosecutor concerned solely the complaints made by the applicants regarding the alleged assaults by male police officers on the way to the Malatya Court House.
The remaining thirteen police officers denied that the demonstrators had been assaulted in the police vehicles on 8 March 2005.
The remaining thirteen police officers stated that the arrested persons had been accompanied by female officers in the vehicles on 8 March 2005.
On 18 April 2005 the Malatya prosecutor examined the video footage submitted to his office by the police and recorded his findings in a report.
In his report of 18 April 2005, the Malatya prosecutor expressed the opinion that the demonstrators had tried to break the police cordon and march on 8 March 2005.
In his report of 18 April 2005, the Malatya prosecutor expressed the opinion that the police officers had not behaved in an arbitrary manner on 8 March 2005.
In his report of 18 April 2005, the Malatya prosecutor expressed the opinion that the use of force by the police officers on 8 March 2005 had not been excessive.
On 12 May 2005 the Malatya prosecutor decided not to prosecute the police officers involved in the events of 8 March 2005.
In his decision of 12 May 2005, the Malatya prosecutor stated that the second applicant, Ms Refika Meltem İspir, had been unable to recognise the police officer who had sprayed her with tear gas.
In his decision of 12 May 2005, the Malatya prosecutor stated that the applicants had gathered in the area without having sought prior permission.

In his decision of 12 May 2005, the Malatya prosecutor stated that in dispersing the unauthorised demonstration, the police officers had been impelled to resort to the use of force in order to apprehend the applicants because they had resisted arrest and insulted the police officers.
In his decision of 12 May 2005, the Malatya prosecutor stated that other than the applicants' unsubstantiated allegations, there was no evidence justifying the prosecution of the police officers.
